messages.text:
Hi Support team,

I flashed HarloOS onto my BS-4 and I feel the power supply is a bit underpowered.

It is a 350w, but at stock voltage and frequency, the device is pulling 95% (334.2w) of rated power.

I had ordered the overclocking bundle; does this come with a higher rated power supply?  Shouldn't it be running at 75% of the rating?  The skinny power cord for the power supply gets pretty warm.

Thank you,
Scott

[cid:4f08be73-2543-4883-aebb-f55006ad9def]
Handed to the team · I cannot confirm the Overclocking bundle PSU's wattage / BS-4 compatibility, and

Hi Scott,

Thanks for the screenshot. I opened it: HarloOS at stock settings (650 MHz, 1150 mV), 17.7 TH/s, ASIC temp 43.5 °C, VR temp 59.8 °C, and the Power bar you circled at 334.2 W, 95% of MAX 350 W. Good news first: 17.7 TH/s is close to the 18.2 TH/s you worked out on the 9th, and the board draws about the same power as before. So the low reading you had back then looks like a counting problem, not dead chips.

On the power supply, I think the 95% looks worse than it is. That 334.2 W is labelled "Estimated wall power". HarloOS calculates it from what the board measures, plus an allowance for conversion losses. The figures the board actually measures are on the line below: 11.6 V at the input and 22.7 A of regulator input current. That works out to about 263 W, which is what the power supply is really delivering. A PSU's 350 W rating normally refers to what it delivers, not what it pulls from the wall, so yours is running at about 75% of its rating. That's the margin you expected. The other readings add up too: 230.8 W reaches the chips, so the board's regulators are about 88% efficient.

There's still not much headroom, though. Overclocking raises the draw quickly, so I wouldn't overclock on this 350 W supply. Overclocking is always at your own risk, and it may void warranty coverage if it causes damage.

About the warm cord: at 115 V the miner pulls only about 3 A from the outlet, so the cord should feel about room temperature, slightly warm at most. Please check that both ends are pushed all the way in and that the cord isn't coiled or bundled. Ideally it should go straight into a wall outlet, not a power strip or extension cord. If the cord or plug gets hot to the touch, feels soft, changes colour or smells, unplug the miner and stop using it until we've looked into it. If you have a plug-in power meter, its reading would also show us how accurate the HarloOS estimate is.

On the Overclocking bundle: I can't confirm its wattage or whether it's meant as a higher-rated supply for the BS-4. I've passed that question, your readings and the warm cord to JD, our hardware lead. The team has it and someone will reply in this thread with an answer, usually within one business day. If you want a faster answer, JD and the community are very active on Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf (mention @nullhashrate).

Best regards, Hal
